text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] HIGH: ALB target health failing in eu-central-1b for service redwood-api (consistent 5xx healthcheck responses). Auto-escalation -> page to on-call. <http://console.aws.amazon.com/elb/home?region=eu-central-1|ALB: redwood-api-euc1>
alex_sre: I'm paged, taking lead. seeing ~40% of targets in tg-redwood-api-euc1b marked unhealthy over last 3m. spikes in 502/504 from healthchecks. app metrics show increased latencies for eu clients.
maria_infra: seeing lots of SYN retries across instances in eu-central-1b, kernel conntrack counters climbing on a couple hosts. might be network flapping between AZ B and the ALB control plane.
kevin_runtime: no recent deploys to the service. runtime logs show repeated "upstream reset" on the nginx sidecar. past hour we've had a few host reboots in that AZ due to underlying EC2 host maintenance.
sam_prod: support is getting customer reports about timeouts from EU region. any ETA for mitigation? the largest affected customers are EU enterprise tenants.
alex_sre: quick impact call: markers -> 502 spike from EU, some requests failover to other zones but weighted routing keeps a lot hitting eu-central-1b. Route53 health checks are passing because edge health is fine; it's ALB->target issue.
jordan_support: customers seeing 30-40% error rates on POST /v1/generate. Escalating to enterprise success teams, adding status page note draft.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-374. Command runbook link: https://internal.redwood/ops/incidents/INC-2026-374
maria_infra: I've SSHed into a couple affected instances. conntrack table at 98% on i-0a1b2c3d; dropping new connections. running: sudo conntrack -S shows high TCP_ESTABLISHED counts. Increasing conntrack max now: echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
kevin_runtime: reconfigured ALB target group healthcheck timeouts to 10s (was 5s) and healthy threshold from 3->5 to reduce flapping temporarily. This will slow fail detection but reduce oscillation.
alex_sre: running a small traffic shift to eu-central-1a and eu-central-1c by adjusting Route53 weights via emergency plan. Will move 40% away from 1b. Updating weights now.
alex_sre: Route53 change submitted: set eu-central-1b weight 20 -> 50? wait typo. corrected: reducing 1b weight 70->30, 1a 15->35, 1c 15->35. changes in flight, should propagate in 60s.
aws-status-bot: AWS Notification: "We are investigating network connectivity issues affecting a subset of instances in eu-central-1b." Link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/abc-123
sam_prod: posting initial status page note: "We are investigating increased errors for EU customers in eu-central-1. Engineers are running mitigations and shifting traffic. We'll update in 15 minutes." pinging customer success.
jordan_support: adding affected customer list to incident doc. I've DM'd the on-call contact for our top 5 EU customers.
kevin_runtime: scaling up replacement targets in 1b is risky while conntrack is saturated. instead launching new instances in 1a/1c and registering them with ALB.
maria_infra: conntrack bump applied, validated with sudo cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max -> 262144. watching counters now; dropping rate reduced.
alex_sre: after weight shift + conntrack bump, 502s dropped from 38% -> 8% in 12 minutes. still seeing intermittent failures for long-poll requests.
kevin_runtime: added an ALB stickiness tweak to reduce churn during recovery (sticking cookies off for 30s). also increased target deregistration delay to 45s to let in-flight requests finish.
sam_prod: any need to fail traffic to another region (e.g., eu-west-1) for critical customers? that is heavier lift but possible for top 3 customers.
alex_sre: Not yet. prefer to keep inside region. if error > 15% for next 20m we'll start cross-region failover for named customers.
ops-handoff-bot: On-call handoff requested in 40m. @maria_infra and @kevin_runtime will take the 2nd shift.
maria_infra: I'm staying on to monitor for 2 hours. will follow up with sysctl persist change so conntrack bump survives reboots.
jordan_support: created support banner and updated status page with "Partial degradation in eu-central-1; mitigations in progress". added note for enterprise contacts.
alex_sre: reaching out to AWS support with trace of affected ENIs and instance IDs. attaching packet captures and conntrack dumps.
aws-status-bot: AWS updated: "We identified elevated control plane retries in eu-central-1b affecting instance networking; mitigation in progress." ETA not provided.
kevin_runtime: rolling planned replacement hosts for the saturated underlying hypervisors in 1b; draining and reprovisioning minimal-impact machines now.
alex_sre: primary mitigation (conntrack bump + Route53 weight shift + scale in other AZs) holding. Error rate stable at ~6% for last 10m. Requesting incident severity to move from SEV2->SEV3 pending continued improvement.
sam_prod: agreed to SEV3 if <10% errors and no major customers impacted. keeping status page updated.
ops-handoff-bot: Handoff reminder: next on-call in 40m is @maria_infra. Please post a short runbook in thread before handing over.
maria_infra: runbook notes: 1) monitor conntrack: sudo conntrack -S; 2) if >85% reapply bump and investigate long-lived TCP sessions; 3) Route53 weights rollback: use emergency DNS playbook; 4) prefer scaling in other AZs vs cross-region failover.
alex_sre: prepping timeline for postmortem: root cause likely AWS instance networking/control-plane issue in eu-central-1b causing conntrack exhaustion on our hosts leading to ALB target flapping. collecting logs to attach.
jordan_support: all enterprise customers notified with guidance. one customer requested immediate cross-region failover—supporting that request as an opt-in manual action.
kevin_runtime: confirm: we'll keep the conntrack persistent change and schedule host reprovision for tomorrow morning in 1b. will also request AWS RCAs and monitor their incident updates.
alex_sre: wrapping up active mitigation. monitoring window 60m. next update in 30m or earlier on changes. Great job team. :thumbsup:
ops-handoff-bot: Handoff executed at 1795559000 to @maria_infra. Thread closed from initial responder for now."
